sources.title: Pedestrian Comfort Guidance for London (Pedestrian Comfort Level Guidance, First Edition)
sources.extract: PDF text extracted locally (rounds 1 and 2; pp.9-14, 17-21, 25). Footways: ppmm = people per hour / 60 / clear width; clear width = total width minus 0.2 m kerb and 0.2 m building buffers minus furniture and its buffers, and gaps under 0.6 m (standard body ellipse) are unusable. Figure 8 bands: A+ under 3, A 3-5, A- 6-8, B+ 9-11 (recommended minimum for all area types), B 12-14, B- 15-17, C+ 18-20, C 21-23, C- 24-26, D 27-35, E over 35. p.12: vitality such as cafe seating may compensate for a lower level, 'not lower than C+ at peak'. Figure 9 (p.14) rates five area types (High Street, Office and Retail, Residential, Tourist Attraction, Transport Interchange) for peak and Average of Maximum Activity on rows A, B+, B, B-, C+, C-, D, E (no separate C row); the text layer is garbled, so the cells were decoded in round 2 from the page's vector fills and re-decoded independently by a second reviewer in r3 (agrees); a rendered-image check is outstanding. Crossings (pp.17-21): relative pph = pph / share of cycle available to cross; arm and island bands A+ under 3 to E over 35, B- (15-18) recommended; island queue rows: two recommended, three acceptable at busy times, four or more very crowded. Appendix B (p.25): recommended total footway width 2.9 m (under 600 pph), 4.2 m (600-1,200), 5.3 m (over 1,200 up to about 2,000 pph). London research; no Vancouver calibration.

sources.title: Commute Trip Reduction, TDM Encyclopedia
sources.extract: Re-opened round 2. 'Proximity to quality transit service tends to increase program effectiveness.' Measured context rows: Vancouver Cambie Corridor 1994-1998 surveys (single-occupancy drivers 'dropped by 1.6%', transit use up about 25%; the unit of the 1.6% is not stated), Bellevue WA downtown worksites 1993-2001 (drive-alone 73% to 59%), Station Tower Surrey (nearly 50% of employees use alternatives, 50 parking spaces avoided). Spack and Finkelstein 2014 (measured): TDM buildings 34-37% less traffic than ITE average rates, 17-24% fewer parking spaces. Rye 2002 and Boarnet 2014: worksite programmes cut peak auto trips 4-20%, usually under 10% without financial incentives. Best Workplaces for Commuters survey: about 15% with incentives, about 7% information only.

sources.title: M/M/c queue
sources.extract: Stability needs rho = lambda/(c mu) below 1. Gives the Erlang C probability of waiting and mean wait in queue Wq = C/(c mu - lambda). Assumes Poisson arrivals and exponential service times.

modules.name: Person-trip generation and mode split
modules.effort: M (about 2 weeks; loading and documenting baselines by trip end dominates; MVP is the static table with scenario fallback, no Monte Carlo; employment-density, trip-rate and destination-share rows due 7 Nov)
modules.design_question: How many person-trips will the program generate per day and in the peak hour, by use, purpose and mode, using a mode split matched to each use's trip end?
inputs: Layer 0: GFA by program tag (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public, amenity)
Layer 0: dwelling units, unit mix, hotel keys
Site area and the brief's 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum (input check)
Office employment-density row (m2 GFA per job; source, year, basis) and person-trip rate rows per employee, dwelling, hotel room and retail m2, each with a source or a SCENARIO flag

Baseline mode-share table loaded by the user, one row per trip end (residence, destination), each with source, year, sample size, confidence interval, date accessed and a driver_passenger_split flag; optional user-entered 'unsourced scenario' rows
Optional SITE output: distance to nearest rapid-transit station
Optional scenario: event or weekend profile (BC Place, Entertainment District)

parameters.name: GFA per use (Layer 0) and brief minimum
parameters.relationship: More office or retail GFA raises employees and visitors, so person-trips rise roughly in proportion; more residential GFA raises resident trips. The brief's 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum fixes a floor of about 103,200 m2 on this block.

parameters.name: Floor area per employee
parameters.relationship: Lower area per job (denser office) raises employee count and commute trips for the same GFA. No Vancouver row is sourced, so it stays an editable preset and the output stays SCENARIO until a row with source, year and basis is loaded (due 7 Nov).

parameters.name: On-site attendance factor (hybrid work)
parameters.unit: % of employees on site per weekday
parameters.relationship: Lower attendance cuts commute trips and peak flows for the same employee count. No sourced value; 2021 place-of-work data are COVID-affected. Editable preset shown on every office result.

parameters.name: Baseline trip end (residence or destination)
parameters.relationship: Residents use residence-end shares; attractions need destination-end shares (region-wide diary tabulated by destination, 2008 Vancouver-CBD; or Census place-of-work). A residence-end share on attractions overstates walking: red 'basis mismatch' badge and watermark, no block.

parameters.name: Baseline vintage
parameters.relationship: Vintage moves office commute shares and on-site attendance: 2008 diary (CBD, old), 2011 (Vancouver/UEL), Census 2016 (pre-COVID), 2021 (COVID-affected), 2023 dashboard (residence-end). The year is shown on every share.

parameters.name: Trip rate per person, unit or room by purpose
parameters.relationship: Higher rates scale every downstream flow linearly. Resident reference: 2.65 weekday trips per person (2008 diary, 95% CI 2.63-2.67). Employee, hotel and retail rates have no sourced Vancouver value and stay SCENARIO until a row is loaded (7 Nov).

parameters.name: Internal capture between uses (default OFF in CBD mode)
parameters.relationship: Zone shares already include short walks between nearby uses, so removing internal trips first double-discounts external trips. Switch on only in an ITE vehicle-trip pathway with NCHRP 684 pair rates (not opened).

parameters.name: Mode split vector by purpose and trip end
parameters.relationship: Moving share from auto driver to walk or transit lowers vehicle trips, parking demand and kerb pressure but raises station and footway flows, feeding P09-M03 and P09-M04. Each row carries a driver_passenger_split flag; rows are sourced or labelled scenario.

parameters.name: Auto occupancy (combined-auto rows only)
parameters.relationship: Used only where a row gives one combined 'auto' share; TransLink diary rows split driver and passenger, so no occupancy applies. Reference (2011 screenlines, through trips included): 1.24 regional, 1.17 AM peak, 1.25 CBD. Editable, team-applied.

parameters.name: Peak accumulation factor
parameters.unit: share of daily arrivals parked at once
parameters.relationship: Parking demand = auto-driver vehicle arrivals x factor, so staggered stays and turnover lower stall demand. No source; the default 1.0 is a logical upper bound, labelled 'upper bound', never an estimate.

parameters.name: Distance to nearest rapid-transit stop
parameters.relationship: The VTPI table (Vernez Moudon and Stewart 2013) prints +0.15 for walking and +0.29 for transit against distance, contradicting expectation. Show the printed sign; any direction rule is a labelled team assumption in sensitivity runs only.

parameters.name: Land-use mix and street connectivity
parameters.relationship: Higher mix and intersection density are associated with more walking (elasticities 0.15 and 0.39) and less vehicle travel (-0.09 and -0.12). Use as sensitivity tests, not stacked multipliers.

parameters.name: Parking supply per use (from P09-M02)
parameters.relationship: Fewer or priced stalls lower drive-alone share; parking-management measures typically cut requirements 10-30% each in car-oriented contexts. Treat as a scenario, not a default.

parameters.name: Peak-hour share of daily trips (K) and directional split
parameters.relationship: A higher K raises station, entry and kerb loads; office is inbound in the AM, residential outbound. Vehicle hourly shape comes from screenline tables, transit from TSPR hourly data; person-trip K stays a team assumption.

parameters.name: Event or weekend profile
parameters.relationship: Event crowds and weekend visitors to cultural and public uses add walk and transit trips outside the weekday-only diary and shift the peak away from commute hours. No sourced rate; scenario input only.

metrics.name: Baseline-basis check (trip end)
metrics.good: Every use runs on a row whose end matches its trip end: residence-end for residents; destination-end (diary tabulated by destination, Census place-of-work, cordon counts) for attractions
metrics.bad: Any attraction use on a residence-end row (for example CBD-resident shares): red 'basis mismatch' badge and watermark; result still shown as a team assumption, not blocked
metrics.value_status: tool rule (S15 weighting by residence; destination tabulations exist in S65)
metrics.flag_ref: r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: Trip Diary cannot give destination splits; r1 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: Trip Diary shares for all uses
metrics.basis: Round 3 corrects the reason: a residence-weighted, region-wide diary can be tabulated by destination (2008 report: Vancouver-CBD). The real limits are coarse geography, residents only, sample size and vintage. Sub-regions 21 and 22 still have only a few hundred sample households each.
metrics.method: Compare each loaded row's basis field with the use's trip end; show sample size and confidence interval beside every share.

metrics.name: Data-pack readiness per use
metrics.good: Every use has a same-basis mode-share row, an employment-density or trip-rate row and a driver_passenger_split flag, each with source id, year, sample size and CI
metrics.bad: A use runs on user-entered rows: watermark 'unsourced scenario', and all dependent outputs (M02, M03, M04, M05, M07) inherit it; a pack not two-person checked by 7 Nov ships as SCENARIO, never partial green
metrics.basis: Replaces the round-1 hard block so office trips exist on launch day; the status strip lists READY, SCENARIO or EMPTY per output and OWNER MISSING per sprint deliverable.
metrics.method: Count rows by status; propagate the weakest status downstream.

metrics.name: Claimed deviation from the same-basis baseline
metrics.good: 0 points (modelled share equals the same-basis baseline), or a deviation carrying a linked justification from M07 or M02 that passes its own evidence check
metrics.bad: A deviation claimed without a linked justification, or any comparison against a different-basis share (regional average)
metrics.basis: Replaces the circular test (modelled share equals the loaded baseline); regional average allowed only for residents on a residence basis.
metrics.method: Modelled share minus same-basis baseline share, shown with basis, year and sample size.

metrics.name: Sustainable-mode share versus City target (context only)
metrics.good: Shown against the target with its year and scope; no pass/fail
metrics.bad: No fail threshold: the target is city-wide, not a site test (50% preset removed)
metrics.value_status: unverified (Transportation 2040 and climate plan not opened; two-thirds recalled)
metrics.basis: Reviewer notes Transportation 2040 set its target for 2040 and a later plan reportedly moved two-thirds to 2030. 1997 plan targets in Memon 2009 are historical.
metrics.method: Plot modelled share beside the target with target year, scope and a source badge.

metrics.name: Auto-driver share of office commute trips
metrics.good: 25% or less (about one in four, the 1997 downtown planning basis)
metrics.bad: Above 40% (editable preset)
metrics.basis: Good value is the 1997 Transportation Plan basis reported by Memon (2009), possibly superseded. Bad value is a preset. Compare against a destination-end baseline.
metrics.method: Auto-driver commute trips divided by office commute trips.

metrics.name: Internal capture share of all trips (ITE pathway only)
metrics.good: Inside the NCHRP 684 pair ranges for the use mix (ranges to be loaded)
metrics.bad: Above the upper bound of those ranges (over-claiming); any non-zero value in CBD person-trip mode
metrics.basis: Default OFF in CBD mode to avoid double-discounting; method calibrated for ITE vehicle trips.
metrics.method: Internal trips divided by total trips from the pair matrix.

metrics.name: Non-residential GFA versus the brief's 9.0 FSR minimum
metrics.good: 1.0 or more (at least 9.0 x site area; about 103,200 m2 for 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2)
metrics.bad: Below 1.0 (brief minimum not met); residential, hotel-only or non-employment GFA does not count
metrics.value_status: brief fact as supplied in the project context; PDF not re-opened here and its file name, version, date and page not yet recorded
metrics.applicability_status: source-stated once the clause is cited
metrics.basis: Downgraded from verified in r3: S63 is unopened. Brief states a minimum 9.0 FSR of non-residential, high-employment floor area (office, commercial). Which uses count (for example hotel) is a PROG judgement.
metrics.method: Sum GFA of tagged office and commercial uses divided by (9.0 x site area).

metrics.name: Parking-demand arithmetic (no occupancy on driver trips)
metrics.good: Parking demand = auto-driver vehicle arrivals x peak accumulation; occupancy is applied only to a combined 'auto' share; unit tests pass for both driver_passenger_split paths
metrics.bad: An occupancy multiplier applied to driver trips (inflates stall demand by about 17-28% at occupancy 1.17-1.28); a peak accumulation below 1.0 without a user entry
metrics.flag_ref: r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: ParkingDemandEstimate = auto-driver commuters x occupancy
metrics.basis: Auto-driver trips are vehicles already. S56 defines occupancy as persons per vehicle including the driver; the diary (S65) reports driver and passenger separately.
metrics.method: Two test cases: (a) split row: vehicles = driver trips; (b) combined row: vehicles = auto-person trips / occupancy; stalls = vehicles x peak accumulation.

metrics.name: Destination-end reference shares for Vancouver-CBD (2008, context only)
metrics.unit: % of resident person-trips ending in Vancouver-CBD
metrics.good: Shown beside the model with year, geography and basis; AM peak transit 45.9%, auto driver 33.1%; PM peak transit 24.8%, auto driver 33.2%; no pass/fail
metrics.bad: Used as a threshold, or presented as a current share
metrics.value_status: sourced (S65 Exhibits 3.4 and 3.5 column totals; shares computed here; block order inferred)
metrics.basis: AM 06:31-09:30: persons 125,230, transit 57,460, auto driver 41,430. PM 15:31-18:30: persons 73,090, transit 18,130, auto driver 24,250. Auto passenger, walk and bike are inside the remainder (21.0% AM, 42.0% PM). Printed expanded trips carry no CI.
metrics.method: Column totals for destination Vancouver-CBD divided by the all-persons column total.

visualization: Stacked bars of daily external person-trips by mode for each use, with the loaded baseline of the matching trip end drawn as a tick on each bar, a red outline where the basis mismatches and a diagonal 'unsourced scenario' watermark on scenario rows
24-hour stacked area of person-trips by mode with the peak hour shaded, an in/out toggle and a dashed weekend or event overlay
Sankey from use to purpose to mode; link width is trips; hover shows factor value, source badge, basis, sample size and status colour (verified, team assumption, FALSE ASSUMPTION)

Gauge of non-residential GFA against the 9.0 FSR minimum, and a launch-day status strip listing every P09 output as READY, SCENARIO or EMPTY plus OWNER MISSING per sprint line; the spread band is labelled 'scenario spread from assumed ranges' and greyed when more than half the factor ranges are team assumptions
outputs: PersonTripTable (use x purpose x mode x hour, in/out, with basis tag per row)
PeakHourDemand {transit_in/out, walk_in/out, bike, auto_driver, taxi_TNC, servicing_vehicles}
ModeShareSummary with provenance, basis, sample size and driver_passenger_split per factor
ParkingDemandEstimate (auto-driver vehicle arrivals x peak accumulation; no occupancy multiplier) for P09-M02 and P09-M07
NonResidentialGFACheck for PROG
LaunchStatus {output, READY | SCENARIO | EMPTY}
modules.method: 1) Daily person-trips per use T = driver x rate (employees = GFA / m2 per job x attendance; residents = units x persons per unit; occupied keys; programmed visitors). 2) Pick the mode-share row by trip end: residence-end rows for residents; destination-end rows for attractions (diary tabulated by destination, Census place-of-work, cordon counts). No same-basis row: the user enters scenario shares, results are coloured as team assumptions and watermarked 'unsourced scenario'; nothing is blocked. 3) Internal capture OFF by default. 4) Vehicles: if the row splits driver from passenger, auto-driver trips are vehicles; only a combined 'auto' share is divided by occupancy. 5) Parking demand = auto-driver arrivals x peak accumulation (default upper bound 1.0, labelled). 6) Peak hour = daily x K x directional split. 7) Check non-residential GFA against 9.0 x site area. 8) Optional 1,000-draw Monte Carlo labelled 'scenario spread from assumed ranges'. Every factor shows source id, basis, sample size and status colour.
modules.human_judgment: Choice of benchmark zone, vintage and basis for each use; whether to claim a better split than the baseline (needs a linked justification); attendance and employment-density assumptions; attendance for civic, cultural, public and event-day uses with no standard rate; which uses count toward the 9.0 FSR; the narrative linking mode split to design moves.
modules.limits: The Trip Diary weights households by residence region-wide, so destination-end tabulation is possible but coarse (2008: Vancouver-CBD; 2011: Vancouver/UEL), resident-only (2008 excludes non-resident, commercial and passenger-serving trips), sample-limited, weekday-only and dated; the 2023 dashboard's destination filter is unconfirmed. Census place-of-work is commute-only, usual mode; 2021 is COVID-affected. Employee density and trip rates are unsourced. ITE is paywalled.

modules.name: Parking, loading and bicycle by-law check
modules.effort: M (rule-pack transcription and two-person checking dominate; computation is trivial; Sections 4, 5 and 6 packs due 7 Nov with a same-day go/no-go)
modules.design_question: Does the scheme provide the accessible, visitor, loading, passenger and bicycle spaces the Parking By-law requires and stay within any downtown maximum, with every rule traceable to a clause?
inputs: Layer 0: GFA by use, dwelling units and sizes, hotel keys, child-care capacity if tagged
Employee count from P09-M01
Provided counts or modelled spaces: car, accessible and van-accessible, Class A/B/C loading, passenger spaces, Class A/B bicycle, EV-ready stalls
Optional: cyclist route polyline from street to the Class A room
User-imported rule packs (JSON), one per by-law section (4, 5, 6): section id, consolidation date, SHA-256 checksum, checker initials

parameters.name: Minimum off-street parking
parameters.relationship: No minimum applies downtown (since 2018) or citywide (since 30 June 2024), so supplying fewer stalls cannot create a by-law deficiency. Accessible and visitor stalls still count.

parameters.name: Downtown maximum (non-residential; residential row if any)
parameters.relationship: More non-residential GFA raises the ceiling in proportion; stalls above it need a relaxation. A search extract gives 1 per 115 m2 (s.4.2.5); text not opened; the VTC block's Downtown-area membership is an organiser Q&A item (send 28 Oct, due 3 Nov).

parameters.name: Class B and C loading requirement by use, GFA and units
parameters.relationship: More units or GFA triggers extra Class B or C bays in steps. The 2012 text had none under 100 dwellings and one at 100-299 (old); the current table was not opened.

parameters.name: Passenger-space requirement by use (hotel keys, GFA)
parameters.relationship: Required passenger spaces add kerb or on-site bays that compete with active frontage and push drop-off into the lane. A reviewer reports Section 5 rows including hotels; rate, size and triggers are not confirmed.

parameters.name: Loading bay dimensions by class
parameters.relationship: A larger required bay (Class B 10.2 x 3.4 m in a May 2026 extract versus 8.5 x 3.0 x 3.8 m in 2012) deepens the dock footprint and headroom. Until the Section 5 pack is checked, bays show as outlines without dimensions.

parameters.name: Class A bicycle rate
parameters.unit: spaces per unit, m2 or room
parameters.relationship: Higher rates enlarge the secured room. Sources conflict: 1.25 per unit and 1 per 500 m2 commercial (Council 2008 via Memon), 1.5-3 per dwelling and 1 per 170 m2 office (vendor). Only the official table can settle it.

parameters.name: Class B (visitor) bicycle rate
parameters.relationship: Triggered at size thresholds (vendor: 6 spaces at 2,000 m2 office). More spaces lengthen the rack frontage near entries, competing with footway width.

parameters.name: Cyclist route and room quality
parameters.relationship: Class A needs a secured room with lockers and showers, reached by a route from the street. Long ramps, small bike lifts or a route crossing the dock add area and conflict. Limits come from the Design Supplement (not opened).

parameters.name: EV-ready and car-share rows
parameters.relationship: Any stalls supplied can carry EV-outlet and car-share obligations that size the electrical room in SYST. Memon (2009) called EV outlets voluntary (dated); a reviewer says energized outlets are now likely mandatory, rate to load from Section 4. Until loaded, SYST plans for all supplied residential stalls energized (team assumption).

parameters.name: Accessible and van-accessible parking
parameters.relationship: More parking-using GFA raises accessible stalls; van-accessible stalls need wider aisles and more headroom, enlarging the level plate. Still required after 2024; rate and split not found.

parameters.name: Child-care capacity
parameters.relationship: Adding a child-care facility adds Class A 1 per 17 employees and Class B 1 per 6 FTE spaces, per a June 2024 report extract.

parameters.name: TDM variance and City TDM requirement
parameters.relationship: An accepted TDM plan could once vary loading and bicycle counts case by case (c. 2021 City memo, no longer kept as a source). The City TDM policy was tied to the removed minimums and may have changed; relief is a user entry.

metrics.name: Parking provided versus downtown maximum
metrics.good: At or below 1.0 (at or under the maximum)
metrics.bad: Above 1.0 (relaxation needed)
metrics.applicability_status: team-applied (site membership of Downtown area unconfirmed; organiser Q&A item)
metrics.basis: Section 4 (June 2026) not opened; rate from a search extract.
metrics.method: Provided stalls divided by maximum from the rule pack.

metrics.name: Minimum-parking deficiency test
metrics.good: No minimum applies; fewer stalls is compliant
metrics.bad: Reporting a parking shortfall as a deficiency (corrected false assumption)
metrics.value_status: sourced (S01 vote and 2018 downtown removal; S02 effective date)
metrics.basis: Minimums removed 2018 downtown and 30 June 2024 citywide.
metrics.method: Rule is switched off; shows a corrected-assumption badge if a user rule row tries to enable it.

metrics.name: Loading bays provided versus required, per class
metrics.good: 1.0 or more in each of A, B and C
metrics.bad: Below 1.0 in any class without a documented relaxation
metrics.basis: Section 5.2 table not opened.
metrics.method: Provided bays divided by required bays from the rule pack.

metrics.name: Passenger spaces provided versus required
metrics.good: 1.0 or more against the larger of by-law rows and the queue-model demand from P09-M05
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Reviewer reports Section 5 passenger rows including hotels; not confirmed.
metrics.method: Provided divided by required, with the larger of by-law and queue demand.

metrics.name: Class A bicycle spaces provided versus required
metrics.good: 1.0 or more
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Official table not opened; secondary and 2008 rates conflict.
metrics.method: Provided divided by required.

metrics.name: Class B bicycle spaces provided versus required
metrics.good: 1.0 or more
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Official table not opened.
metrics.method: Provided divided by required.

metrics.name: Bay dimension check
metrics.good: Every modelled bay meets the by-law length, width and height for its class
metrics.bad: Any bay smaller than its class envelope
metrics.basis: Dimensions differ between 2012 and 2026 extracts; no dimension passes to SPAC or STRC until the Section 5 pack is two-person checked.
metrics.method: Compare bay rectangles with the class envelope.

metrics.name: Accessible and van-accessible parking provided versus required
metrics.good: 1.0 or more for each row
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Requirement confirmed to remain (S01, S24); rate and van split not found.
metrics.method: Provided divided by required.

metrics.good: 1.0 or more once the Section 4 row is loaded and checked
metrics.bad: Below 1.0, or SYST sized on the dated 'voluntary' reading (Memon 2009)
metrics.value_status: unverified (reviewer-stated as likely mandatory for residential stalls; Section 4 not opened)
metrics.basis: Rate and non-residential rows unknown; Memon (2009) is dated and the by-law has changed since.
metrics.method: Provided energized stalls divided by required from the rule pack.

metrics.good: Continuous route from street to room that avoids the loading dock and meets the user-entered ramp and lift limits
metrics.bad: Route crosses the dock or exceeds the entered limits
metrics.value_status: assumed (limits entered from the Design Supplement by the user)
metrics.basis: Reviewer gap; Design Supplement not opened.

Paired horizontal bars of required versus provided for loading A/B/C, passenger spaces, bicycle A/B and parking against the maximum, with a line at 100%; bars of unchecked rows are grey

modules.method: Rule-pack engine. Each row stores row type (parking maximum, accessible, van-accessible, visitor, loading A/B/C, passenger, bicycle A/B, EV-ready, car-share, City TDM), use, formula type (per m2, unit, room, employee, step threshold), parameters, rounding rule, clause id, section pack version, status and checker initials. Required count = formula result rounded as the row states, summed over uses; provided counts come from Layer 0 or entry fields; Shapely intersects bay rectangles with class envelopes. City pages block automated access, so packs are versioned per section (section id, consolidation date, SHA-256: Section 4 June 2026, Section 5 May 2026, Section 6 Feb 2026) in one manifest. Every row needs a two-person 'transcription checked' tick; unchecked rows render grey as team assumptions, cannot produce a green badge and pass no dimension to SPAC or STRC.
modules.human_judgment: Whether to seek or argue a relaxation (the brief says justified breaches may be rewarded), reading ambiguous clauses, how much parking to supply when none is required, and trading bay area against active frontage.
modules.limits: Section consolidations carry different dates and may change, so rows go stale quickly. No pack exists until two people have transcribed and checked it (due 7 Nov); until then every row is grey and bays are outlines without dimensions. Required counts depend on GFA definitions at permit stage; CD-1 or district rules can override. The VTC brief calls its documents non-legal, so results are indicative.

modules.name: Transit connection and station-entrance capacity
modules.effort: S for tier 0 (arithmetic, lookup tables, TSPR 2025 loader, user headway; due 13 Nov); M for tier 1 (passage graph, queues, GTFS surge inputs, line context; v1, 10 Dec); L for agent-based validation (roadmap)
modules.design_question: For a chosen proxy station, can the below-grade secondary entrance carry tower, station-patron and through flows comfortably, and what stays unchecked for egress?
inputs: PeakHourDemand transit_in/out from P09-M01 (or P09-M07 adjusted), or a user-entered tower transit trip count
Required: proxy-station choice (an existing station, or a new-station scenario with user-entered lines and headways)

Required scenario: station-patron demand captured by the new entrance (TSPR 2025 hourly alightings and boardings for the proxy station, 2023 kept for comparison, times a user share) and through-pedestrian flow
Layer 0: polyline or polygon of the connection (stairs, escalators, lifts, fare line) with clear widths; tier 0 needs only one clear width
User-entered headway (tier 0) or TransLink GTFS filtered to the proxy station's lines only (tier 1)
User-entered per-line train capacity and line peak-hour-per-direction capacity with source; user-entered stair, escalator and gate capacities

parameters.name: Proxy station and its lines
parameters.relationship: Waterfront loads Expo and Canada lines; Burrard, Granville or Stadium-Chinatown load Expo only; Vancouver City Centre or Yaletown-Roundhouse load Canada only. More lines raise frequency and shrink platoons; a wrong choice distorts every surge.

parameters.name: Clear passage width
parameters.relationship: Wider clear width lowers flow per metre and raises space per pedestrian, moving the link to a better walkway band. Required width equals design flow divided by the flow rate at the chosen band.

parameters.name: Design surge flow per train arrival
parameters.relationship: Alightings per train x entrance share / dispersal time sets the one-to-five-minute surge. Larger platoons from longer headways or bunching worsen the band. Do not multiply hourly flow by a surge factor; that double-counts peaking.

parameters.name: Station-patron demand captured by the new entrance
parameters.relationship: A public entrance serves all nearby patrons, so its flow can exceed tower demand and may govern width. TSPR 2025 8-9 AM alightings (MF, inferred): Burrard 4,306, Granville 3,353, Waterfront 3,974, City Centre 2,246. Share is a scenario.

parameters.name: Through-pedestrian flow
parameters.relationship: Passer-by flow between the plaza, neighbouring sites and the street adds to tower and station flow on the same width and worsens the band. No City pedestrian-count dataset was found.

parameters.name: Entrance choice by walking time
parameters.relationship: Shorter walking time to the new entrance raises its share of station flow. Default is shortest-walk assignment over the passage graph; an optional logit scale is a team assumption. The VTPI mode-choice elasticities are not used here.

parameters.name: Walking speed, counter-flow fraction and effective-width deduction
parameters.relationship: More opposing flow, columns or furniture reduces effective width and lowers speed, raising density. Values come from TCQSM chapter 10, which could not be read, so all are editable assumptions.

parameters.name: Stair, escalator, lift and fare-gate throughput
parameters.relationship: Lower vertical or gate throughput creates queues where the passage meets the platform or fare line. No sourced rates; user-entered from TransLink or TCQSM.

parameters.name: Train headway and capacity per line
parameters.relationship: Shorter headways shrink platoons; bigger consists raise alightings per arrival. Capacity is user-entered; secondary references: Canada Line two-car train 334 comfortable, 400 crush; Expo Mark V five-car 672 regular, 1,207 crush. Read headways from GTFS.

parameters.name: Line peak-hour-per-direction capacity
parameters.relationship: Tower peak-direction riders divided by line capacity give the share of the line used; a higher share means fuller trains. References: Canada Line 15,000 (RFP requirement); Expo 12,000 (pre-2009) to 19,400 (design).

metrics.name: Walkway space per pedestrian on moving links
metrics.good: 1.4 m2 or more (Fruin walkway LOS C or better; editable)
metrics.bad: Below 0.9 m2 (walkway LOS E or worse; editable)
metrics.value_status: unverified (boundaries supplied by reviewer from Fruin 1971; exhibit not read)
metrics.applicability_status: source-stated (TCQSM applies Fruin to station walkways) once read
metrics.basis: 1.4 and 0.9 m2 are walkway-scale boundaries (C/D and D/E), not queuing values. Remaining boundaries to be read from the TCQSM exhibit.
metrics.method: Flow per metre divided by walking speed gives density; invert to space per person; map to the walkway scale.

metrics.name: Queue area per person at stair or fare line (queuing scale)
metrics.good: 0.7 m2 or more (queuing LOS C or better; editable preset)
metrics.bad: Below 0.3 m2 (queuing LOS E or F); 0.3-0.7 shown amber
metrics.value_status: unverified (reviewer scale A 1.2 or more, B 0.9-1.2, C 0.7-0.9, D 0.3-0.7, E 0.2-0.3, F under 0.2; exhibit not read; boundaries such as 0.65 versus 0.7 may differ by edition)
metrics.flag_ref: r1 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: queue area 1.4 and 0.9 m2
metrics.basis: Replaces the earlier use of walkway boundaries (1.4 and 0.9) for queues. Tier 1 only.
metrics.method: Queue length from the cumulative diagram times area per person, mapped to the queuing scale.

metrics.name: Required width divided by provided width (tier 0 comfort check)
metrics.good: 1.0 or less (provided width suffices at the chosen band)
metrics.bad: Above 1.0
metrics.basis: Tier 0 sizes on tower plus station plus through flow with a user headway and a single clear width; labelled 'unverified scale, comfort only, not egress-compliant'.
metrics.method: W_req = design flow / flow rate at chosen band, compared with effective width.

metrics.name: TfL PCL on below-grade passage (removed)
metrics.good: TfL PCL not used underground; used only for street-level footways and crossings in P09-M04
metrics.bad: Applying TfL footway bands (B+ 11 ppmm) to station passages, stairs or fare lines
metrics.value_status: tool rule (the S17 scope statement, footways and crossings only, is sourced)
metrics.basis: TfL guidance covers footways and crossings only; peak-hour basis; it was misapplied to peak-minute station flows.
metrics.method: Rule: any TfL band used on a link flagged underground is labelled team assumption and cannot produce a badge.

metrics.name: Proxy-station headway source check
metrics.good: Only the proxy station's lines are loaded and headways read from GTFS (or user-entered in tier 0) for that station; combined-trunk headways used only at Waterfront
metrics.bad: Combining Expo and Canada trunk headways at a station served by one line, or using the Millennium Line for a CBD station
metrics.value_status: sourced (secondary: S23, S61, S62; GTFS authoritative)
metrics.applicability_status: team-applied (proxy for a hypothetical station; organiser Q&A item)
metrics.basis: Waterfront is the only direct Canada-Expo connection; Vancouver City Centre to Granville is a walk. A new-station scenario is user-entered.
metrics.method: Filter GTFS stops, trips and routes to the proxy station; compute headway by time period with gtfs_kit.

metrics.name: Station baseline vintage and definitions
metrics.good: TSPR 2025 hourly rows are the default baseline, 2023 shown beside them, and MF is labelled 'Monday-Friday average (inferred)'
metrics.bad: 2023 used as the default, or station counts treated as entrance counts or as transfer-free
metrics.value_status: sourced values (S58 rows read); column meanings inferred
metrics.basis: Burrard 8-9 AM alightings 4,306 in 2025 against 3,819 in 2023 (+13%). The TSPR page does not define 'Average', 'MF' or transfer handling.
metrics.method: Load 2025 and 2023 rows for the proxy station; show both with the day-type label.

metrics.name: Tower-added peak-direction riders divided by proxy line peak-hour-per-direction capacity
metrics.good: Context only, no pass/fail: shown with the capacity source and year
metrics.bad: No threshold; flagged amber when line capacity is a placeholder or secondary reference
metrics.basis: First-order TOD question the station-entrance check does not answer; routed to the policy reflection, not scored. Tier 1.
metrics.method: Peak-direction tower transit trips divided by user-entered line capacity per direction.

metrics.name: Platform storage per train arrival
metrics.unit: persons per arrival; m2 per person
metrics.good: Context only: tower plus station alightings per arrival shown against user-entered platform area
metrics.bad: No sourced threshold (TCQSM chapter 10 unread)
metrics.basis: Platform crowding is not computed beyond this arithmetic. Tier 1.
metrics.method: Alightings per train x entrance share, divided by user-entered platform area.

metrics.name: Transit access context: departures within an 800 m walk and destinations reachable in X minutes
metrics.good: Context only: map and counts shown with GTFS feed date and the 800 m radius (Province TOA basis)
metrics.bad: Placeholder when no opportunities layer (jobs, amenities) is loaded; no threshold
metrics.value_status: assumed (radius from S24; opportunities layer not sourced)
metrics.basis: Core TOD measure the critique found missing; GTFS gives supply only, destinations need a user-loaded layer. Tier 1.
metrics.method: Cumulative-opportunities accessibility from the site by walk plus transit with r5py or gtfs_kit and OSM.

metrics.name: Egress hand-off status
metrics.good: Egress report from SYST (NFPA 130 or authority criteria) attached and accepted by the station owner
metrics.bad: No egress report: all width badges withheld and outputs labelled 'comfort only, not egress-compliant'
metrics.basis: Reviewer: platform-evacuation and point-of-safety criteria may govern width regardless of comfort.
metrics.method: Check for an attached egress record; otherwise watermark all outputs.

visualization: Plan-view false-colour of each passage link by walkway band (A dark green to F red), with legend ticks at the band boundaries and a diagonal 'NOT EGRESS-CHECKED' hatch until a hand-off is attached; tier 0 draws a single bar (required versus provided width) instead of a plan
Line chart of queue length at the stair or fare line over a 10-minute train-arrival cycle with storage capacity as a dashed line (tier 1)
Stacked bar of entrance load by source (tower, station patrons, through) with the share of each stated
Schematic of the proxy station's lines with headway per time period, and a bar of tower-added riders against line capacity labelled 'context, secondary capacity source' (tier 1)
Isochrone map of walk-plus-transit access (r5py) with the 800 m walk ring; optional animated agents coloured by density from JuPedSim trajectories (roadmap)
outputs: PassageCapacityReport {link_id, flow, space_per_person, band, required_width, badge_withheld}
StationEntranceLoad (persons per hour by direction and source) for liaison with the station owner and the policy reflection
ConnectionGeometry (typed polyline with widths) for STRC, SYST and SPAC
EgressHandoff {status, standard, assigned_to: SYST} placeholder
ProxyStationManifest {station, lines, baseline year, GTFS date, capacity sources} and LineLoadingContext (tier 1)
CULTHandoff notes for arrival, naming and wayfinding (no metric)
modules.method: Tier 0 (core, 13 Nov): 1) User picks a proxy station or new-station scenario. 2) Demand = tower transit trips (M01/M07 or entered) + TSPR 2025 hourly alightings x user entrance share + through pedestrians; trains per hour from user headway or GTFS. 3) Surge = alightings per train x entrance share / dispersal time; entrance share by shortest walking time. 4) Density = flow per metre / walking speed; map space per person to the walkway scale (editable, unverified boundaries); required width = flow / flow rate at the chosen band. 5) No green width badge; label 'unverified scale, comfort only, not egress-compliant' until an egress record is attached. Tier 1 (v1): link widths on a passage graph from Layer 0, queues at stairs and fare line from cumulative arrivals minus service, line context, platform storage, GTFS headways (gtfs_kit), accessibility isochrones. Optional validation: JuPedSim with PedPy, or SUMO.
modules.human_judgment: Agreement with the station owner on entrance location and share of flow; wayfinding and arrival experience; whether the connection is a public amenity or back-of-house shortcut; structural conflicts; accessible route design (CSA B651 checklist; standard not opened); life-safety egress, which this module does not assess; and co-design with the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations for arrival, naming and wayfinding in the connection (hand-off to CULT, no metric).
modules.limits: Platform evacuation and train-load capacity are not computed; line capacity is user-entered. Walkway and queuing scales are unverified (TCQSM chapter 10 unread). Egress (NFPA 130 or authority criteria) may govern width and is out of scope. The neighbouring station is hypothetical, so proxy results are team-applied. TSPR counts are station-level with undefined 'Average' and 'MF' semantics. GTFS use needs the TransLink legend; run-time download is a design choice, not a requirement.

modules.name: Entry flows, street comfort and route directness
modules.effort: M (MVP by 13 Nov: footway ppmm with the Figure 9 lookup, crossing-arm bands, width quick check, route directness; queue and Poisson runs are v1)
modules.design_question: Do entrances, footways and crossings to the transit plaza stay comfortable at peak for their TfL area type, where do queues spill, and how direct are routes through the block?
inputs: PeakHourDemand (walk, transit, taxi arrivals) from P09-M01 or P09-M07
Layer 0: entrance openings (position, clear width, door count) and the program each serves
SITE: footway and forecourt polygons, total footway widths, street furniture, street classes (arterial, retail high street, lane, transit plaza, mid-block connection)
SITE: signal timings (green man, blackout, red man) and crossing arm and island widths for intersections between the site and the transit plaza
Street network (OSM) with and without the proposed mid-block passages
Optional: pedestrian counts on adjacent footways supplied by the user; optional TfL spreadsheet result for Average of Maximum Activity

parameters.name: Entrance clear width and door count
parameters.relationship: More clear width raises entry service rate and shortens queues; fewer doors for the same arrivals push the queue onto the footway. Service rates are team assumptions.

parameters.name: Arrival peaking (15-minute PHF, shift-start alignment)
parameters.relationship: Aligned shift starts concentrate arrivals; a lower PHF (more peaked) raises peak ppmm and queue spill. No sourced Vancouver factor, so it is a preset, separate from the K share in P09-M01.

parameters.name: Screening or turnstile throughput
parameters.relationship: Slower screening lowers entry service rate, so queues form earlier. No sourced rate was found.

parameters.name: Footway total width, furniture and buffers
parameters.relationship: Narrower clear width raises ppmm for through pedestrians plus entering flow. TfL clear width = total minus 0.2 m kerb and 0.2 m building buffers minus furniture and its buffers; gaps under 0.6 m are unusable.

parameters.name: Background through-flow on the footway
parameters.relationship: More passer-by flow adds to tower flow on the same width and worsens the band; the permitted band depends on the area type's Figure 9 cell. A few 2011 downtown manual counts exist but not for this block.

parameters.name: Area-type mapping of Vancouver street classes
parameters.relationship: Arterial maps to Office and Retail, retail high street to High Street, station-entry footways to Transport Interchange, plaza and civic frontage and event days to Tourist Attraction. A stricter type lowers permitted ppmm and widens the footway needed. Team assumption.

parameters.name: Crossing signal timing and arm width
parameters.relationship: A shorter green-plus-blackout share raises relative pph and so ppmm; a wider arm lowers it. Relative pph = pph / share of the cycle available to cross. London pelican-crossing research; Vancouver phases differ.

parameters.name: Island width and queue rows
parameters.relationship: A narrower island fits fewer people per row, so more rows form while waiting. Two rows are recommended, three acceptable at busy times, four or more very crowded and people cross elsewhere.

parameters.name: Queueing area per person in lobby
parameters.relationship: More area per waiting person keeps queues inside the lobby and cuts spill onto the footway. Area standards (Fruin queuing scale) were not read.

parameters.name: Entry share by frontage (arterial, high street, lane)
parameters.relationship: More entries on the retail high street load that footway and lower its band; entries on the lane relieve the frontage but weaken public-facing activity. A design judgement, not a sourced rule.

parameters.name: Taxi and ride-hail drop-off bays
parameters.relationship: More kerb bays shorten vehicle queues in the lane or street but take footway or frontage. Sized with the kerbside model in P09-M05.

parameters.name: Mid-block connections and entrance spacing
parameters.relationship: A passage that shortens the walk between station entrance, plaza, high street and entries lowers the directness ratio; fewer passages lengthen detours around the block. CMHC 2008 links more direct paths to higher walking share (association only).

metrics.name: Footway PCL at peak by area type (TfL Figure 9 cell lookup)
metrics.unit: ppmm (peak-hour people per hour / 60 / clear width)
metrics.good: B+ or better (11 ppmm or less) at peak in every area type, the TfL recommended minimum (Figure 8)
metrics.bad: Cell rated 'unacceptable' for the area type: High Street and Tourist Attraction C+ or worse (18 ppmm or more); Residential C row or worse at peak (21+); Office and Retail and Transport Interchange D or worse at peak (27+). Cells 'at risk' are amber; values between printed bands take the worse band; Figure 8 band C (21-23 ppmm), which Figure 9 omits, is read as the printed C- row
metrics.value_status: sourced for Figure 8 bands and the B+ minimum; Figure 9 cells decoded from page vector fills, re-decoded independently by a second reviewer in r3 (agrees), rendered-image check outstanding
metrics.applicability_status: team-applied (London footways; Vancouver street classes mapped by the team)
metrics.flag_ref: r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: previous critic's Figure 9 reading (retired); r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: C+ as universal fail line
metrics.basis: Decoded Figure 9 (rows A, B+, B, B-, C+, C/C- as printed 'C-', D, E; peak then Average of Maximum): High Street and Tourist - comfortable to B+, acceptable B, at risk B-, unacceptable C+ and worse. Residential - comfortable to B+, acceptable B and B-, at risk C+ at peak (C+ and C/C- on Average of Maximum), unacceptable beyond. Office and Retail and Transport Interchange - comfortable to B, acceptable B- and C+, at risk C/C- at peak (C/C- and D on Average of Maximum), unacceptable D and E at peak, E on Average of Maximum.
metrics.method: (peak-hour through-flow + entering flow) / 60 / clear width, looked up cell by cell in a 5 area types x (peak, Average of Maximum) x 4 ratings table with amber bands; band C is read as the C- row; the table carries a 'cells unconfirmed' watermark until two users confirm it against the rendered PDF (31 Oct).

metrics.name: Vitality exception (documented)
metrics.good: Not invoked
metrics.bad: Invoked without a written justification, or invoked at worse than C+ at peak
metrics.value_status: sourced (S17 p.12: not lower than C+ at peak)
metrics.basis: C+ is the limit on a vitality exception such as cafe seating, not the general fail line.
metrics.method: Require a justification text and area-type note before any band worse than the Figure 9 'acceptable' cells is tolerated.

metrics.name: Average of Maximum Activity check
metrics.good: Rated acceptable or better for the area type in the TfL spreadsheet
metrics.bad: Rated unacceptable for the area type
metrics.value_status: unverified (spreadsheet not opened; 10-second maxima not public)
metrics.basis: TfL computes this from busiest 10-second samples built into its spreadsheet; the tool cannot reproduce it, so the user imports the result.
metrics.method: Imported rating shown beside the peak-hour band.

metrics.name: Crossing-arm PCL at peak (TfL Step 2) for intersections between site and transit plaza
metrics.good: B- or better (18 ppmm or less), the TfL recommended level for crossing arms
metrics.bad: C or worse (over 18 ppmm): crowding may push people to cross away from the crossing
metrics.basis: The plaza sits diagonally across an intersection, so surface crossings carry transit walk flow the below-grade link does not.
metrics.method: Relative pph = pph / share of cycle (green man plus blackout); ppmm = relative pph / 60 / arm width; band lookup.

metrics.name: Island queue rows on crossings
metrics.good: Two rows or fewer (TfL recommended)
metrics.bad: Four or more rows; three rows are amber (acceptable at busy times only)
metrics.basis: More than three rows encouraged crossing outside the island in the TfL research.
metrics.method: Queue per cycle = relative demand per cycle; rows = queue / people per row from island width and the 0.6 m body ellipse.

metrics.name: Total footway width quick check
metrics.good: At least 2.9 m (under 600 pph), 4.2 m (600-1,200 pph), 5.3 m (over 1,200 pph, to about 2,000)
metrics.bad: Below the minimum for the flow band; smaller totals acceptable only where no street furniture exists
metrics.basis: TfL gives total widths (not clear widths) for early design; the full PCL assessment supersedes it.
metrics.method: Look up flow band, compare with SITE total width, flag furniture presence.

metrics.name: Entrance clear width divided by width required for the target band
metrics.good: 1.0 or more
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Derived from the chosen band's upper ppmm (11 for B+).
metrics.method: Provided width / (peak-hour flow / 60 / band upper limit).

metrics.name: Queue spill outside the property line
metrics.good: 0 m2 at design peak
metrics.bad: More than 0 m2
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no source.
metrics.method: Queue area beyond lobby polygon intersected with forecourt or footway polygon.

metrics.name: 95th-percentile screening wait
metrics.good: 2 min or less
metrics.bad: More than 5 min
metrics.basis: Editable preset; no source.
metrics.method: Poisson arrivals, 200 replications.

metrics.name: Route directness (network distance / straight-line distance) from station entrances, plaza and high street to each public entry, with and without proposed passages
metrics.unit: ratio; walking minutes at user-entered speed
metrics.good: Lower than the same routes without the proposed passages (relative test; no absolute threshold)
metrics.bad: Higher than the without-passage case, or a route that crosses the loading dock or forces a detour around the block
metrics.basis: Human-scale 40% includes connectivity and mid-block connections. CMHC 2008 (via VTPI): walking share about 18% where pedestrian paths are more direct than car routes, 10% with poor connectivity (association, not a threshold).
metrics.method: OSMnx shortest paths on the street network plus Layer 0 passages; ratio per origin-entry pair; Shapely tests for dock conflicts.

visualization: Ground-plane heat-map of predicted ppmm on footways and forecourt using the TfL A+ to E legend, with the area type printed on each segment, a 'cells unconfirmed' watermark until checked, and entry arrows scaled to flow
Entry badges showing band and area-type rating (comfortable, acceptable, at risk, unacceptable) linked to the Figure 9 cell
Crossing bars at each intersection to the plaza coloured by band with island row glyphs
Small-multiple queue-length time series per entry with the lobby capacity line; spill polygons outlined red
Route-directness lines from each station entrance and the plaza to each entry, coloured by ratio, with a with/without-passage difference map
outputs: EntryFlowMatrix (entry x minute, in/out)
SpilloverPolygons for PUBL modules and SPAC
FootwayPCL by segment and area type, and CrossingPCL, for human-scale scoring
RouteDirectness table and map for PUBL
TaxiTNC kerb demand for P09-M05
CULTHandoff notes for arrival, naming and wayfinding on the plaza frontages (no metric)
modules.method: Assign each entry its arrivals per minute from PeakHourDemand with a 15-minute PHF. Footways: clear width = total minus 0.2 m kerb and 0.2 m building buffers, furniture and its buffers (gaps under 0.6 m unusable); ppmm = (through-flow + tower flow) per hour / 60 / clear width; look up the area-type rating in a cell-by-cell Figure 9 table (5 area types x peak or Average of Maximum x 4 ratings); values between printed bands take the worse band and Figure 8 band C reads as the C- row. C+ applies only as the limit on a documented vitality exception. Crossings: relative pph = pph / share of cycle available to cross; ppmm = relative pph / 60 / arm width; island rows from queue per cycle. Add the Appendix B width quick check. Entry queues from cumulative arrival and service diagrams; overflow spills to the forecourt. Route directness by OSMnx and Shapely. Optional Poisson run (200 replications). Station passages are in P09-M03.
modules.human_judgment: Entry sequence and sense of welcome, whether queues are acceptable as gathering space, security stance, activation of ground-floor edges, balancing comfort bands against an intimate street character, and Indigenous co-design (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh) of arrival, gathering, naming and wayfinding on the plaza frontages (hand-off to CULT, no metric).
modules.limits: TfL bands are calibrated to London footways and pelican crossings, not Vancouver or interior spaces. Figure 9 cells were decoded from page geometry (two geometry checks agree) and still need two-person visual confirmation by 31 Oct. No City pedestrian-count dataset was found (2011 screenline reports carry a few manual downtown counts), so through-flow is supplied or assumed. Peaking, screening and service rates are unsourced presets. Static peak only; events and weather are not modelled.

modules.name: Servicing, kerbside and access placement
modules.effort: M for placement checks, Erlang screening and the design-vehicle library (three checked vehicles plus the fire-apparatus slot by 7 Nov); L for swept-path analysis and the SimPy reported value (v1)
modules.design_question: Can deliveries, drop-off, servicing and fire apparatus be handled from lanes and kerbs, with enough bays and storage that trucks never queue onto streets or cross the retail high street?
inputs: Layer 0: massing, program, core and ground-floor footprint
SITE: block edges with street class (arterial, retail high street, lane), mid-block connections and lane width (default 6.1 m, team assumption)
LoadingBayCount and PassengerSpaceCount from P09-M02
Optional DockScheduleDemand from P09-M06 (preset if absent)
Taxi and ride-hail kerb demand from P09-M01 and P09-M04
Design-vehicle library: Class B, Class C, City refuse truck and a fire-apparatus slot
City open data: lanes, one-way streets, bikeways, truck routes, right-of-way widths

parameters.name: Number of loading bays c (by class)
parameters.relationship: More bays lower utilisation and the probability that an arriving truck waits (Erlang C). Stability requires arrival rate below c times service rate.

parameters.name: Truck arrival rate lambda in the busiest hour
parameters.relationship: Rises with retail, hotel and residential GFA and unit count, and raises utilisation and queue length. No sourced Vancouver freight-trip rate was found (screenline truck shares are traffic shares), so it is an editable preset.

parameters.name: Arrival process (random versus booked)
parameters.relationship: Booked, scheduled deliveries cut waiting and queue variance versus random arrivals. Erlang C assumes Poisson arrivals and exponential dwell, so it is a screening approximation that can err in either direction.

parameters.name: Dwell time per truck
parameters.relationship: Longer dwell (move-ins, bulk deliveries) raises utilisation in proportion; consolidation or booking shortens it.

parameters.name: Delivery-hour profile
parameters.relationship: Regional truck volumes peak midday and the PM-peak hour is lower than the AM; shifting deliveries off the PM peak lowers lane conflict then but raises midday dock load. Shape only; a person reads the 2014 truck survey for it (sprint, 7 Nov).

parameters.name: Design vehicle by loading class (library)
parameters.relationship: Larger design vehicles need longer bays, wider turning areas, more headroom and a deeper dock. Slots: Class B, Class C, City refuse truck (checked by 7 Nov) and fire apparatus (unverified); swept-path results stay greyed until the slot is checked.

parameters.name: Fire-apparatus envelope and access route
parameters.relationship: A longer or wider apparatus and larger turning radius at the lane and frontage enlarge setbacks and podium cut-backs, and may govern lane geometry on a 244-305 m tower more than delivery trucks (reviewer). Vancouver Fire Rescue Services and building by-law criteria not opened.

parameters.name: Access position along the lane (distance from nearest intersection)
parameters.relationship: Closer to the intersection leaves less on-site storage for waiting trucks, so queues spill onto the street sooner. No Vancouver spacing standard was obtained.

parameters.name: Vehicle-access frontage by street class
parameters.relationship: More access width on the retail high street breaks the retail edge and adds conflict points; lane access protects the public realm but loads the lane. The 1997 plan sought better truck access to downtown lanes.

parameters.name: Lane width and turning radii for the design vehicle
parameters.relationship: Narrower lanes or smaller radii raise the setback or turntable needed to enter the dock. City data give legal right-of-way widths only; default 6.1 m (20 ft, commonest unmarked lane-like value near Burrard and Georgia; unit inferred), a flagged team assumption.

parameters.name: Dock clear height and ramp slope
parameters.relationship: Taller design vehicles need more structure and floor-to-floor height at dock level. By-law envelope values are in the 2012/2026 text and the 1988 supplement, none opened.

parameters.name: Kerb demand: passenger loading, taxi, ride-hail, courier, accessible drop-off
parameters.relationship: The larger of by-law passenger spaces (P09-M02) and queue-model demand governs. More kerb bays on the high street break active frontage; lane bays load the lane. Frontage is allocated across arterial, high street and lane.

parameters.name: Number of curb cuts crossing footways
parameters.relationship: Each added crossing adds a pedestrian-vehicle conflict point and lowers footway comfort and safety along that frontage.

metrics.name: Dock utilisation rho = lambda / (c x mu)
metrics.good: Below 0.70 (preset)
metrics.bad: 1.0 or more (queue grows without bound)
metrics.basis: Instability at rho of 1 or more is queueing theory; the 0.70 comfort level is a preset.
metrics.method: Arrival rate over service capacity.

metrics.name: Probability that a truck must wait (Erlang C, screening approximation)
metrics.good: 0.10 or less
metrics.bad: More than 0.30
metrics.basis: Editable presets; formula from S22 assumes random arrivals and exponential dwell, so it is labelled a screening value; from v1 the SimPy run with lognormal dwell and a booked-arrival option is the reported value.
metrics.method: Erlang C formula.

metrics.name: 95th-percentile truck queue versus on-site storage
metrics.good: Queue no longer than on-site storage
metrics.bad: Queue longer than storage (spills onto street or lane)
metrics.basis: Geometric logic; storage length from the plan; simulation by SimPy (MIT).
metrics.method: SimPy run with lognormal dwell and optional booked arrivals.

metrics.name: Vehicle access on the retail high street
metrics.good: 0 m
metrics.bad: Any curb cut on that frontage
metrics.basis: Preset; Vancouver downtown lane-access guidance was not opened.
metrics.method: Sum of access widths by edge class.

metrics.name: Swept-path clearance for the library design vehicle
metrics.good: Design-vehicle envelope clears all structure and lane edges
metrics.bad: Any intersection of envelope and obstruction; result greyed out (no pass/fail) while the vehicle library is unchecked
metrics.basis: Geometric test; clearance margin editable; envelope is a simplified kinematic sweep (Shapely, BSD-3-Clause).
metrics.method: Shapely intersection of swept envelope with obstacles.

metrics.name: Fire-apparatus swept-path clearance (hand-off to SYST)
metrics.good: Apparatus envelope clears structure and lane edges along the access route
metrics.bad: Any intersection; no pass/fail shown while the apparatus slot is untranscribed (greyed)
metrics.value_status: unverified (apparatus dimensions and access-route criteria not opened; BC Codes site not reachable)
metrics.basis: Reviewer gap: fire access can govern lane geometry on a supertall. Criteria come from Vancouver Fire Rescue Services or building by-law access-route rules, to be transcribed.
metrics.method: Same sweep as the delivery vehicles with the apparatus slot; result passed to SYST as FireAccessRoute.

metrics.name: Kerb bays provided versus the larger of by-law passenger spaces and queue-model demand
metrics.good: 1.0 or more
metrics.bad: Below 1.0
metrics.basis: Passenger-loading rule rows are not confirmed; queue demand is a preset.
metrics.method: Provided bays divided by max(required, modelled demand).

metrics.name: Delivery-hour profile basis
metrics.good: Hourly shape and light/heavy split read by a person from the 2014 truck survey or the screenline hourly tables and labelled 'screenline-type counts, not building rates'
metrics.bad: Screenline truck shares used as building arrival rates, or the 2014 survey left unread because tooling could not parse it
metrics.value_status: sourced shape (S56, S57); 2014 survey unread by the packet author
metrics.flag_ref: r3 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: 2014 truck survey not readable
metrics.basis: The reviewer reports the 2014 survey downloads (20.9 MB, encrypted PDF) and opens in a standard viewer; the block was in the fetch tool.
metrics.method: Manual transcription into an hourly share table with year and source; tick-checked.

visualization: Block plan with edges coloured by street class and candidate access points as pins: green on lane, amber on side street, red on high street; designated truck routes drawn as a heavy line

Swept-path polygons for each library design vehicle (including the fire apparatus) over the dock plan, red fill where the envelope hits structure; greyed with a 'vehicle library unchecked' label until the library is checked
Bar chart of probability of waiting versus number of bays with the design point and thresholds marked, labelled 'Erlang C: screening approximation'
Gantt strip of dock occupancy across the day with queue length overlay, and a kerb-allocation strip per frontage (passenger, taxi, courier, accessible)

modules.method: Placement: classify every block edge from SITE (lane, arterial, high street), list candidate access points and score by street class and distance from the intersection. Sizing: treat the dock as an M/M/c queue (arrival rate lambda, mean dwell 1/mu): utilisation, Erlang C probability of waiting and Wq = C/(c mu - lambda) as a screening value; a SimPy run with lognormal dwell and optional booked arrivals gives the 95th-percentile queue against storage (reported value from v1). Geometry: pick the design vehicle per class from the checked library (TAC designations, City refuse truck, fire apparatus), sweep its envelope along the entry path with minimum turning radius and lane width, and intersect with lane edges, columns and ramps using Shapely. Kerb bays = larger of by-law passenger spaces and queue demand. Count curb cuts and conflict points per frontage, rank access options, and hand the fire-apparatus sweep to SYST.
modules.human_judgment: Where servicing sits relative to the public realm and the lane's character, whether lanes become activated shared spaces, operating regime (booking, hours), neighbour effects, how much conflict is acceptable against a larger dock footprint, and the fire-access route agreed with the fire department.
modules.limits: Arrival rates, dwell times and thresholds are presets; no sourced freight-trip rates (screenline truck shares are traffic shares; the 2014 truck survey needs manual reading). modules.name: Transportation demand management scenarios
modules.effort: S (tier 1 measure table, context selector and floor check; Monte Carlo is optional)
modules.design_question: Which TDM measures could this tower credibly adopt, how far could they cut auto trips and parking demand given its transit-rich context, and what by-law relief might they support?
inputs: ModeShareSummary and PeakHourDemand from P09-M01, including the lowest same-basis observed CBD share (floor)
ParkingLoadingBikeLedger from P09-M02
User-selected TDM measures and intensity (subsidy %, parking price, and so on)
Evidence context selector: CBD, within 660 ft of a station, or elsewhere
Layer 0: end-of-trip facilities (bike rooms, showers) and car-share stalls
City TDM requirement row (plan, measures or points, financial security) with version date, status 'unverified pending the City bulletin'

parameters.name: Evidence context (CBD, near-station, elsewhere)
parameters.relationship: Select the evidence row matching the site. Ewing's predicted effect of a 100% subsidy is 35% in a CBD, 25% within 660 ft of a station and 10% elsewhere (50% subsidy: 20, 15, 10), so transit-rich contexts get larger predicted effects, not smaller.

parameters.name: Transit or rideshare subsidy level
parameters.relationship: Higher subsidy lowers commute auto trips. Sacramento model predictions by context (above), not observed results, with no stated baseline.

parameters.name: Parking price or cash-out
parameters.relationship: Higher price lowers driving: elasticity -0.1 to -0.3, so a 10% rise cuts driving 1-3%. Commuter cash-out reduces automobile commuting 15-25%. Evidence is from car-oriented contexts.

parameters.name: Cost-recovery (full-price) parking
parameters.relationship: Moving from free to cost-based parking reduces parking demand 10-30% and drive-alone commuting 10-30% in the evidence base; the effect shrinks where parking is already priced and auto share is low.

parameters.name: Programme bundle (information, services, incentives)
parameters.relationship: Comprehensive worksite bundles cut 4-20% of peak auto trips (Rye 2002; Boarnet et al. 2014); US survey bundles with incentives about 15% versus about 7% for information only; programmes without financial incentives usually under 10%.

parameters.name: Shared parking and unbundling
parameters.relationship: Sharing lets 20-40% more users per space. Each management measure typically trims requirements 10-30%, a full package 30-50%; TDM buildings in Minneapolis-St Paul needed 17-24% fewer spaces than ITE rates imply.

parameters.name: End-of-trip facilities and car-share
parameters.relationship: Secure Class A rooms, showers and car-share stalls support cycling and low-car living. The City has required car-share since at least 2009. No quantified effect found; used as qualitative toggles.

parameters.name: Observed same-basis floor
parameters.relationship: Adjusted auto-driver share cannot fall below the lowest same-basis CBD share loaded in M01 (candidate: 2008 diary, CBD-destination AM peak 33.1%, all purposes, dated). A lower claim needs a stated justification and shows as a team assumption.

parameters.name: Optional sensitivity factor k
parameters.relationship: k = site auto share / evidence auto share (cap 1) tests a more sceptical claim. It is not applied by default, because the cited source predicts larger percentage effects in transit-rich centres. Evidence auto share is an editable team assumption.

parameters.name: Overlap discount between measures
parameters.relationship: Measure effects overlap, so summing overstates results. The combined reduction is capped at the evidence range for the chosen bundle type, not added.

parameters.name: Delivery consolidation
parameters.relationship: Fewer, consolidated deliveries lower arrival rate lambda and dock utilisation in P09-M05. No sourced percentage was found.

metrics.name: Claimed reduction in peak-hour auto-driver commute trips (context-matched evidence)
metrics.good: Up to 20% (comprehensive worksite bundles with financial incentives, measured in US metros), or up to the Ewing predicted value for the matching context (CBD 35%, near-station 25%, elsewhere 10% at 100% subsidy), labelled predicted
metrics.bad: Above 37% (highest result cited; measured against ITE average rates in Minneapolis-St Paul, a car-oriented baseline, not against a CBD baseline), or any claim that takes the adjusted auto-driver share below the same-basis observed floor, which binds first; 20-37% shown amber
metrics.applicability_status: team-applied (US, Sacramento and Minneapolis-St Paul evidence; no transit-rich Canadian baseline)
metrics.flag_ref: r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: k-scaling (also r1 flag on VTPI ranges)
metrics.basis: Round 2 drops k-scaling as the default; evidence rows are chosen by context. The 37% line is labelled 'reduction versus ITE rates, not versus a CBD baseline' (r3). Measured downtown rows (Cambie Corridor, Bellevue 73% to 59% drive-alone, Station Tower Surrey) report mode shares, not trip reductions, and are shown as context.
metrics.method: Compare the capped combined effect with the evidence row for the site context; show predicted-or-measured and region beside each value; apply the observed floor.

metrics.name: Claimed parking-demand reduction
metrics.good: 30% or less (typical per measure 10-30%)
metrics.bad: Above 50% (top of the 30-50% package range)
metrics.flag_ref: r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION: k-scaling (also r1 flag on VTPI ranges)
metrics.basis: VTPI parking-management ranges applied to a CBD baseline are team-applied; the k scaling used in round 1 is removed (optional sensitivity only). Baseline demand is vehicles x peak accumulation from P09-M01 (r3).
metrics.method: Adjusted parking demand versus baseline, with optional k sensitivity.

metrics.name: Financial-incentive content of the bundle
metrics.good: At least one price, cash-out or subsidy measure included
metrics.bad: Information-only bundle (about 7% effect in the US survey)
metrics.value_status: sourced (S19 Best Workplaces for Commuters survey)
metrics.basis: Survey figures as cited by VTPI under conservative assumptions.
metrics.method: Check measure list for incentive types.

metrics.name: City TDM requirement met (policy view)
metrics.good: Required plan elements present once the City row is loaded and checked
metrics.bad: Row missing or unchecked: result shown as 'City policy view not verified'
metrics.basis: Storeys reports the TDM policy was tied to the removed minimums and staff plan to lower financial expectations downtown.
metrics.method: Rule-pack row check; reported beside the evidence view.

visualization: Waterfall from baseline auto-driver trips through each measure to the adjusted value, whiskers for low-high effect, a red band beyond 37% and below the observed floor, and an 'evidence context: predicted or measured, region' label on each bar
Before-and-after stacked mode-share bars with the City target as a context line and the observed floor as a dotted line
Evidence table: measure, context row, effect range, source badge, status colour, predicted versus observed, evidence region
Line chart of parking demand versus stalls supplied
outputs: AdjustedModeSplit and PeakHourDemand_TDM for P09-M03, M04 and M08
ParkingDemandAdjusted for P09-M02
TDMPlan (measures, effects, sources, City-policy row status) for the policy-reflection board
DeliveryConsolidationFactor for P09-M05
JustificationLinks for the M01 claimed-deviation test
modules.method: Start from baseline auto-driver commute trips and parking demand in P09-M01. For each selected measure take low, central and high effect values from the evidence row matching the site context (CBD, near-station, elsewhere), each tagged predicted or measured with its region. Combine multiplicatively with an overlap discount, then cap at the evidence range of the chosen bundle type. Optional sensitivity: scale by k = site auto share / evidence auto share (cap 1), labelled team assumption. Apply the reduction to commute trips only; visitor and servicing trips are unchanged. Floor the adjusted auto-driver share at the lowest same-basis CBD share loaded in M01. Recompute auto-driver trips, parking demand and the Class A bicycle uplift; report the parking and loading relief that could be argued in a variance next to the City TDM row. Output a TDM plan skeleton. Optional 1,000-draw Monte Carlo labelled scenario spread.
modules.human_judgment: Which measures fit the operator and tenants, commitments the design team will make, equity of parking pricing and subsidies, and whether to argue for a by-law variance.
modules.limits: Effect sizes are US or Sacramento results, predicted or measured against car-oriented or ITE baselines; the Ewing CBD column is a prediction. Measured downtown rows give mode shares, not trip reductions. They apply to commute trips only. The City TDM policy, tied to the removed minimums, was not opened. Measures need an operator; the tool cannot enforce commitments.
